reports.title: Qnity Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results, Raises Full-Year Financial Guidance

guidance.heading: Guidance for Full Year 2026
section: Qnity is raising full‑year guidance based on strong third‑quarter performance and continued momentum in the business.

desk.headline: Sales up 22% to $1.56bn; adjusted EPS $1.46 beat $1.18 estimate; 2026 outlook raised again

other.label: Adjusted free cash flow
other.change: vs $207m pro forma a year ago

results: Sales rose 22% to $1.56bn, all from higher volumes (prices flat), as chip and AI-server demand stayed strong.
Interconnect Solutions (circuit-board and packaging materials) grew 30% and Semiconductor Technologies grew 15%; Asia Pacific, about 80% of sales, rose 24%.
Adjusted EPS jumped 55% to $1.46, but GAAP EPS fell 14% to $0.87 on spin-off related IT and transformation costs ($53m) and higher interest expense ($64m vs $14m).
Gross margin improved to 47.8% and the adjusted EBITDA margin to 32.3% from 29.0% (pro forma).
Nine-month buybacks were $75m and dividends $50m; cash stood at $1.12bn against $4.0bn of long-term debt.

guidance.summary: Qnity raised its full-year 2026 outlook for the third quarter running: sales $5.77-5.83bn, adjusted EPS $4.95-5.05 and adjusted free cash flow $800-900m, all above the ranges given in August.

points: The CEO said materials are becoming key to chip performance as the industry moves to "shrink and stack" designs.
AI-linked products (thermal, advanced packaging, AI circuit boards, about 30% of Interconnect) grew more than 50%; advanced-node chip materials grew 25%.
Management lifted its outlook for chip-factory wafer starts and pointed to a similar pace in 2027, with over 15 advanced fabs due to start production within a year.
Analysts pressed on reported data-centre project delays and the pace of AI spending, the main concern raised.
The company keeps investing where it sees visible customer demand; capex of $290m so far trails a $450-470m full-year plan.
call.source: Press release (Exhibit 99.1); Earnings Whispers call summary via Finviz (4 Nov 2026); 24/7 Wall St. (4 Nov 2026)

watch: Whether AI data-centre build-outs slow, which would hit Interconnect growth
Q4 delivery against the raised outlook and the usual year-end inventory caution at customers
Fall in spin-off and IT separation costs that are still weighing on GAAP profit and cash flow
